FreshHarvest Foods - Q3 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the FreshHarvest Foods Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, please do not use your telephone keypad during the presentation portion of the call. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss FreshHarvest Foods' Q3 results. Joining me on the call are Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Jenkins, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Growth Officer; and Raj Patel, Chief Supply Chain Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Mike.

Mike Thompson (CEO):
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q3. We delivered strong performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures.

Today, I'll be focusing on four key areas: capital expenditure plans and priorities, EBITDA margin performance and key factors, progress on sustainability initiatives and goals, and discussion of pricing actions and revenue growth management strategies.

First, regarding capital expenditure plans and priorities: We're maintaining a disciplined approach to investing in growth, efficiency, and resilience amid commodity inflation and supply challenges.

Second, concerning EBITDA margin performance and key factors: Our margins expanded meaningfully, driven by mix improvements, cost controls, and productivity gains across segments.

Third, in terms of progress on sustainability initiatives and goals: We've advanced significantly on our ESG commitments, delivering both environmental impact and bottom-line savings.

Finally, looking at discussion of pricing actions and revenue growth management strategies: Our targeted pricing and RGM efforts fueled robust organic growth while safeguarding profitability.

Overall, we are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah to provide more detail on our financial results and expand on these priorities.

Sarah Jenkins (CFO):
Thank you, Mike. As Mike mentioned, we achieved solid results in Q3. Net sales were $2.83 billion, representing an 8% increase year-over-year. Gross margin was 38.4%, impacted favorably by pricing and productivity but tempered by commodity inflation. Operating income was $520 million, and earnings per share were $1.25. We are managing our costs effectively and continue to invest in key growth initiatives.

Our balance sheet remains strong with $1.2 billion in cash and marketable securities. We are committed to returning value to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

Let me now expand on those four priorities Mike highlighted, starting with our capital expenditure plans and priorities. Good morning again, everyone, and thanks for joining our Q3 earnings call for FreshHarvest Foods. As we look ahead to FY2024 and beyond, our CapEx strategy is sharply focused on driving sustainable growth, boosting operational efficiency, and keeping us ahead in the Food & Beverage industry's evolution. We're tackling a challenging backdrop with ongoing inflation in key commodity inputs like cocoa and dairy, which are up 15% year-over-year according to the latest FAO indices, evolving consumer demand for healthier, premium, and eco-conscious products, and lingering supply chain issues similar to those from the 2022 Ukraine conflict.

For FY2024, we're targeting total CapEx of $475 million, up a measured 8% from $440 million in FY2023, which equates to roughly 4.2% of our projected net sales of $11.3 billion. This is more conservative than peers like Mondelez or General Mills, who run at 5-6% of sales, thanks to our excellent 95% free cash flow conversion and a goal of over 12% ROIC on new spends. We've run scenarios accounting for potential 10% jumps in palm oil prices or extended Red Sea shipping delays, all while keeping our leverage below 2.5x net debt to EBITDA.

Breaking it into our four main priorities, with some regional specifics and projects:

Maintenance and reliability CapEx takes 35%, or about $166 million, flat year-over-year. This keeps our 120 facilities worldwide humming at over 92% capacity utilization, avoiding the $20 billion in industry downtime losses noted by McKinsey last year. In North America, we're upgrading old equipment in snack plants with IoT sensors for predictive maintenance on extruders used for items like HarvestCrunch granola bars, cutting unplanned outages 25% in test runs. Over in EMEA, $40 million goes to updating bottling lines for AquaVita low-sugar drinks, adopting hygienic designs like Danone's to meet tougher EU recyclability rules and extend shelf life.

Capacity expansion gets 30%, around $143 million, up 15% year-over-year. With Asia-Pacific beverages set for 7% CAGR through 2028 per Euromonitor—far outstripping North America's 2%—we're putting $80 million into a new greenfield aseptic plant in Vietnam for plant-based options like OatFlex milks, similar to Unilever's Indonesia moves, adding 200 million liters to chase the $15 billion ASEAN alt-dairy opportunity. In the U.S., $35 million expands our Midwest frozen foods site with IQF lines for veggie-focused meals, riding the 12% private-label premium trend at places like Kroger. Latin America sees $28 million for beverage manufacturing in Brazil to buffer coffee bean swings that hurt competitors like JDE Peet's.

Innovation and sustainability takes 25%, or $119 million, rising 20% year-over-year. With 68% of consumers ready to pay 10% more for green F&B per NielsenIQ, we're investing $50 million in vertical farming tie-ups, like Nestlé's with AeroFarms, for steady greens in FreshBowl meals, slashing water use 90% and carbon by 40%. $40 million covers solar and biogas upgrades at 15 plants, pushing toward 30% renewables by 2026, beating Coca-Cola's waste goals. On the tech side, AI precision fermentation from Ginkgo-style pilots speeds fermented protein snack development from 24 to 12 months.

Digital transformation and supply chain resilience rounds out at 10%, or $47 million, up 25%. After pandemic-driven 20% inventory bloat from SKU explosion, our SAP S/4HANA upgrade with ML demand sensing—like PepsiCo's—will trim 15% of our 5,000 SKUs and lift turns to 8x. $20 million builds blockchain for cocoa and palm traceability to meet EU deforestation rules and woo Gen Z. In APAC, robotics in Singapore palletizing cuts labor costs 18%.

These spends are front-loaded 60% in H1 FY2024 for quicker payback—average 2.5 years, IRR over 15%. We favor high-margin beverages at 28% EBITDA versus snacks at 22%, with a 70/30 organic-to-M&A mix, including our $150 million tuck-in for a Mexican pouch maker. We can scale back 20% if volumes weaken to protect our BBB+ rating.

This CapEx builds our edge in the $8 trillion F&B space heading toward health, sustainability, and efficiency, fueling 10-12% EPS CAGR to 2027.

Next, our EBITDA margin performance and key factors. This quarter, we hit 22.5%, up 170 basis points year-over-year from 20.8% and 60 basis points sequentially—our sixth straight quarter of gains, proving portfolio strength against 12-15% rises in cocoa, sugar, and dairy per FAO.

By segment: Beverages, 45% of revenue, reached 25.8% from 23.2%, thanks to premium mix in ElectroPure zero-sugar electrolytes grabbing share in the $15 billion functional market versus Gatorade and BodyArmor. Pricing added 450 basis points, countering 3% volume softness in sodas like PepsiCo's experience.

Snacks & Confectionery, 35% of revenue, steady at 21.1% despite 8% cocoa hikes, via 70% hedging at $4,200/ton below $5,800 spot, plus automation from our $150 million CapEx—like Topeka robotics boosting throughput 25% for 120 basis points COGS relief.

Health & Nutrition, 20% and fastest-growing, jumped to 28.4% from 24.9%, on 6% volume plus 5% pricing in plant-based bars and keto snacks, riding millennial upgrades in a category to $100 billion by 2027 per NielsenIQ.

North America fueled 80% of gains at 24.2% via premium Everyday Essentials and probiotic yogurts taking 2 share points in $50 billion alt-dairy. EMEA slipped to 19.8% from 20.5% on 7% energy spikes and UK snack weakness like Unilever's. APAC at 21.5% held via China e-com teas up 15% on Tmall.

Pillars: Price/mix/volume with +4.2% pricing, +1.8% mix offsetting 1% volume; supply chain via Global Sourcing cutting dairy 9% and palm premiums 5% under RSPO, AI forecasting lifting turns to 8.2x and freeing $200 million working capital; SG&A at 12.3% from zero-based budgeting and TikTok ROI 3x TV. FX trimmed 30 basis points from USD strength in LATAM.

We see 22-24% margins in FY24, with $300 million for plant-based capacity, sugar-reduced R&D for EU HFSS, and M&A like $450 million nut butter deal for the $8 billion nut space. Hedged 60% mitigates 20% inflation risks.

Shifting to progress on sustainability initiatives and goals. Before deeper financials, an update on sustainability, core to our strategy at FreshHarvest Foods, a plant-based beverage and snack leader with AquaPure almond milks, TerraCrunch bars, and EcoBrew coffees. Our 2019 'Nourish Planet' framework aligns with SBTi and UN SDGs.

Across five pillars:

Sustainable sourcing: 97% palm oil (150,000 tons) RSPO Mass Balance, up from 85%, ahead of Unilever/Nestlé; 92% Rainforest Alliance coffee from Vietnam/Colombia with regenerative farms; 88% sustainable cocoa via Barry Callebaut. North America at 99% via almond integration, APAC 92% via Indonesia partnerships. Cut sourcing costs 12% with precision ag like drones.

Climate action: Scope 1/2 down 28% (450,000 tons CO2e) on 65% renewables—solar in California, biomass in Brazil. Scope 3 intensity -22%; on track for 45% cut by 2030. Indigo Ag pilot sequesters 1.2 tons/hectare on 50,000 U.S. acres; EU wheat localization cuts transport 18% for CBAM.

Water stewardship: Intensity to 2.1 L/L, beating 2025 goal; replenished 115% via Central Valley projects. India Pune zero discharge recycles 85%, saving $4.2 million.

Circular packaging: 62% portfolio at 30% PCR, rPET at 50% vs. 25% average; virgin plastic -25%; blockchain for 20%; mono-pouches cut UK/EU waste 40%. 100% reusable/recyclable/compostable by 2025.

Community: Upskilled 25,000 farmers for 20% yields/15% incomes; 90% zero landfill, food waste +35% to biogas.

Saved $28 million YTD—8% energy, 5% waste; green SKUs +22% at 12% premiums; NPS 72 vs. 65 peer. $150 million in 2024 for AI/satellite carbon tracking to net-zero 2040.

Finally, our pricing actions and revenue growth management strategies. In Q3, disciplined pricing at 6.2% average and RGM drove 9% reported/7% organic growth—best in two years—shielding margins in inflation.

Pricing responded to 15% cocoa, double-digit dairy/oils (25% COGS). Beverages: 7-9% on Fresho Fizz and VitaQuench, elasticity -1.8 to -2.2 for 65% realization. Snacks: 5.5%, premium Indulge Elite shift +2.1 points mix; flat on 15% EDLP private label.

RGM integrates pricing/promos/innovation/channels for NRRIG: 4.8 points price/mix vs. 2.2 volume dip (IRI soda -3%). AI dashboard cut trade spend 80bps to 14.2%.

North America (45%): 7.1% price/mix, club/e-com +18%; no shrinkflation on hero chips, private label loss 1.2 points. EMEA 5.8%, LactaFree oat +22%. APAC 3.9%, StreetSmart sachets +14% Indonesia. LATAM 4.2%, local coffee hedges FX 40%.

FY24: Premiumization—divest 8% low-RGM, 15 new items to 25% mix; AI pricing at ZIP level +22% hit rate; e-com 12%, app AOV +15%, foodservice RPM +9%.

Q4 5-6% price/mix for 6-7% organic; elasticity -2.0, VPI 92/100.

For the full year, we are reaffirming our guidance for net sales of $11.3 billion and EPS growth of 10%.

Now, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
[Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please proceed.

John Smith (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your business?

Mike Thompson (CEO):
Good morning, John. Inflation remains a headwind, particularly in cocoa up 15% and dairy, but our hedging—60% on key inputs—plus pricing actions averaging 6.2% and supply optimizations have more than offset it, delivering margin expansion. We're well-positioned with diversified sourcing.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with JPMorgan. Please proceed.

Emily Chen (JPMorgan):
What are your plans for plant-based milks and what is the expected impact on volume growth?

Lisa Chen (Chief Growth Officer):
Thanks, Emily. Our OatFlex and alt-dairy expansions, including the Vietnam plant, target 7% APAC CAGR. We expect 15-20% volume uplift in the $15 billion ASEAN market, with premium pricing driving mix benefits and overall organic growth contribution of 2-3 points next year.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please proceed.

David Lee (Morgan Stanley):
How are you managing supply chain disruptions?

Raj Patel (Chief Supply Chain Officer):
Good question, David. We're enhancing resilience with $47 million in digital CapEx, including SAP ML for demand and blockchain traceability for cocoa/palm to meet EU regs. Regional manufacturing like Brazil coffee and robotics in APAC cut risks, maintaining 92% utilization despite Red Sea issues.

Operator:
Our last question comes from Maria Gonzalez with Barclays. Please proceed.

Maria Gonzalez (Barclays):
What is your outlook for the rest of the year?

Sarah Jenkins (CFO):
Maria, thanks. We're on track for full-year organic growth of 6-7%, margins 22-24%, with Q4 price/mix 5-6%. CapEx rolls out as planned, sustainability savings accelerate, and RGM keeps us agile amid moderating inflation. Risks like commodities are hedged, supporting 10% EPS growth.

Operator:
I would now like to turn the call back over to Mike for closing remarks.

Mike Thompson (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your continued interest in FreshHarvest Foods. We are focused on executing our strategy and delivering strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
